{"query": "current credit balance expiry per grant ledger credit applications invoice Support policy", "results": [{"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/support-console-credit-ledger-2027.json", "chunk": "3/3", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Credit Ledger (April 2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-04-01", "text": "## Expiry dates
Each grant has its own expiry date, shown on its grant entry. When a customer holds several grants, give the balance and the expiry date of each one, not only the total.
## Applying credits
Credits are applied automatically to the next invoice, oldest expiry first. Support doesn't move credits between invoices or accounts.
## Why the change
`credit_grants` stored one remaining amount per grant, updated in place, so a wrong update left no history. The ledger keeps every change, which Finance needs for revenue recognition and audits.
## Questions
Ask in #support-billing. Page owner: Dev Patel.
_Last reviewed 2027-04-01._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/support-console-credit-ledger-2027.json", "chunk": "2/3", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Credit Ledger (April 2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-04-01", "text": "## Requests about credits
Answer balance, expiry and what-credits-can-pay-for questions from the ledger and the credits policy, with no case. Paying credits out as cash, refunding them, restoring an expired credit, or any exception to the policy isn't Support's to grant: explain the policy, promise nothing, and open a Finance case with the ask.
## Entry types
| Entry | Meaning |
|---|---|
| grant | A credit was added: promotional, goodwill approved by Finance, or a duplicate-charge credit |
| application | Part of a grant was used to pay an invoice |
| expiry | The rest of a grant expired on its expiry date |
| reinstatement | Finance put back an amount that was applied in error |
A grant's balance is the sum of its entries; a customer's balance is the sum across their grants that haven't expired."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/packaged-tiers-credit-conversion-guidelines-2024.json", "chunk": "5/8", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Packaged tiers and credit conversion guidelines", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-20", "text": "billing_examples: Example 1 (Growth): Growth subscription includes 150M tokens. Customer used 230M tokens in month. Calculation: 150M included -> 80M overage * $0.00035 = $28. Example 2 (Business with Dedicated): Business includes 3 reserved-GPU-months. Customer consumed 220 compute-hours. Reserved credits cover 216 hours (3*72). Burst billed for 4 hours * $12 = $48.
migration_plan: 1) Identify impacted customers via feature flag 'legacy-credit-holder' and export balances (Product/Finance). 2) Run a one-time conversion script to calculate token-equivalents and store as 'legacy_credit_balance' in billing table. 3) Notify customers with 30/14/7-day emails describing conversion and their new included balance. 4) Offer a temporary 10% discount on first 3 months when they switch to Growth/Business tiers. 5) Close migration window after 90 days and disable legacy billing path."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/marketplace-credit-memo-limits-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Marketplace Credit Memos: Approval Limits (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-04", "text": "title: Marketplace Credit Memos: Approval Limits (2027)

body: ## Scope
Credit memos that Partnerships raises through the AWS or GCP marketplace for marketplace-billed customers. They are not Support console credit notes, and they don't apply to direct Redwood invoices; Support's own limit is in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix.
## Limits
- Up to $1,000 per memo: Partnerships.
- Above $1,000: FP&A.
_Last reviewed 2027-02-04._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-credit-balances-2026.json", "chunk": "2/2", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Reading Credit Balances", "status": "published", "date": "2026-05-06", "text": "## Quoting a balance
- Look up the account, then query `credit_grants` by account.
- Quote the total and, for each grant, its remaining amount and `expires_on`.
- A grant with no `expires_on` does not expire.
_Last reviewed 2026-05-06._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "19/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "### Example 2: Service credit for metering bug impact
- Trigger: confirmed double-counting bug for streaming retries
- Remediation: credit equal to overbilled amount for the impacted invoice period
- Required: Support ticket, query evidence, RevRec sign-off, and customer communication stating the credit is specific to the identified issue
## Exception log (policy-impacting only)
- 2026-02-22: Clarified that credits apply to **billed tokens** (post-dedupe/cache attribution) to align with meter hardening work and reduce invoice disputes. Owner: Finance/RevRec."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "4/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Policy summary (non-negotiables)
1. **All discounting and credits must be recorded in systems of record** (Deal/Account + Billing) and have an approver trail.
2. **No retroactive price changes** to already-invoiced usage without Finance + Legal approval and a documented RevRec assessment.
3. **Credits apply to billed usage as computed by billing meters** (not customer-estimated counts).
4. **Discount stacking is limited** (see “Stacking rules”). Any exception is an exception request.
5. Credits must have an **expiry date** unless explicitly waived by Finance (rare; requires CFO approval).
6. Any term that could be interpreted as “free usage” must include a clear definition of **the exact meter(s)** and the application order (see “Contract language requirements”)."}]}

{"query": "March 2027 invoice credits applied invoice contents usage invoice lookup policy credits", "results": [{"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "4/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "## Credits and the close
Credit notes issued before BD4 are applied to the invoice being issued; later credit notes are applied to the next invoice. The credit ledger shows the date each one was applied.
## Year-end
The December 2027 close runs on the same business days. Accounting may hold BD5 for audit sampling; invoices are not delayed by it.
## Questions
Ask in #billing-ops. Close calendar owner: Emily Stone. Metering freeze: Logan Wright."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "(continued) ## Monthly close calendar
Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.
## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.
Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "19/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "### Example 2: Service credit for metering bug impact
- Trigger: confirmed double-counting bug for streaming retries
- Remediation: credit equal to overbilled amount for the impacted invoice period
- Required: Support ticket, query evidence, RevRec sign-off, and customer communication stating the credit is specific to the identified issue
## Exception log (policy-impacting only)
- 2026-02-22: Clarified that credits apply to **billed tokens** (post-dedupe/cache attribution) to align with meter hardening work and reduce invoice disputes. Owner: Finance/RevRec."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "9/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "### Application order (standard)
On each invoice, the billing system applies adjustments in this order:
1. **Included usage** in the customer’s package/free tier (if applicable)
2. **Contracted unit prices** (including any negotiated discount)
3. **Credits** (promotional/contracted/service), applied to the eligible usage subtotal
4. Taxes and non-creditable line items
Important: credits offset charges; they do **not change recorded usage quantities**.
### Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens
If the meter spec distinguishes cached vs uncached billed tokens, credits apply to the final **billed** quantities after cache and dedupe logic. Any customer-visible statement about caching must use approved language from Legal (see related page)."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "10/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### Customer notifications
Minimum notification set (must be enabled for all paid workspaces):
- 80% included usage (warning)
- 100% included usage (soft limit)
- 110% included usage (approaching hard limit)
- Invoice preview available (see month-end preview process)
---
## Credits, refunds, and disputes (packaging interaction)
### Credits application order
Unless an order form specifies otherwise:
1) Included usage
2) Promotional or sales-issued credits
3) Overage charges
### Refunds/credits policy (high level)
- Billing disputes are governed by the dispute window in the MSA/order form.
- Any retroactive adjustment impacting recognized revenue requires Finance approval and must be documented with an audit trail.
- Support may issue customer goodwill credits only per the approvals matrix in the Discounts/Credits policy.
---"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "6/7", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Audit trail
Every adjustment is recorded on the invoice it changes, with the approver's name and the evidence above. Console credit notes record the issuing agent and the reason code automatically. Adjustments issued outside the console are logged by Billing Ops in the adjustments register within one business day.
## Revenue recognition
Credits reduce the transaction price of the period they relate to. Adjustments over $10,000, or any adjustment to a closed quarter, need the Controller's sign-off before they are issued so that revenue can be restated where needed. Support-issued duplicate credits are always within an open period's tolerance and need no separate sign-off."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-quality-standards-2027.json", "chunk": "2/3", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Quality Standards 2027: Confirm Before You Write", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-29", "text": "## No early promises
- Don't tell a customer a credit is likely or coming before the console confirms it's a duplicate.
## Why
In the 2026 quality review, most complaints about credits weren't about the amount: customers hadn't known a write was about to happen, or had been told a credit was coming before the console confirmed anything. These standards fix both.
## Saying what you're about to do
Name the action, the invoice line and, for a credit, the amount. For example: "I'll issue a credit note for the duplicated line L2 on invoice INV-…, for the full amount of that line. Shall I go ahead?""}]}

{"name": "payments-and-credits", "steps": "Failed card payment
1. lookup_account; ask_developer for invoice_id, error_code, time_of_issue and timezone if not given. Convert the failure time to UTC.
2. search_knowledge for the current payment-failure procedure and for payment-processor incident notices (status cards: "INC card payments failing"). Compare the failure time (UTC) with each published window; the start and end instants count as inside. The time decides, not the decline code.
3. Inside a window: no case. Name the incident, say the payment failed because of it, that it will be retried automatically, when the retries complete, that they need do nothing and no late fees apply. If this notice gives no completion date, derive the processor's usual schedule from ALL past payment-processor notices (search "INC card payments failing" and read each one's window end and "last retries completed" date). For each, call date_calculator(window_end_date, completion_date) and compare calendar_days and business_days; the measure that is the same across every notice is the schedule (a notice ending on a Friday shows whether weekends count). Apply it with date_calculator to this window's end date and state the date. Work this out once, carefully, and keep the same answer on follow-up questions unless you find a notice you had not read.
4. Outside every window, failed again after retries completed, or charged twice after retries: Billing Ops case with invoice number, decline code and failure time (load team-handoff).
5. Bank-transfer / invoice-pay accounts and overdue invoices: search the collections pages for their schedule.

Card changes and card data
- Never ask for, repeat, or store card digits (full, partial, last four, or spoken). If the developer shared one, tell them not to send card details to Support.
- Search the current card-update procedure; follow it (e.g. the customer changes the autopay card themselves in Console billing settings, no case). A card shared during a payment failure doesn't change how the failure is routed.

Credit balances
1. lookup_account: credits are computed from the credit ledger (sum of each grant's entries; expired grants excluded). Search the current credits policy for which table Support quotes.
2. Quote each grant's remaining balance and its own expiry date, plus the total. Mention that credits apply automatically to the next invoice if the policy says so.
3. Cash-out, refund, restoring expired credit or any exception: explain the policy, promise nothing, and open a Finance case only if the developer asks for it (load team-handoff)."}
